S.FORM: ma-faðaq m-apa buna masa kawi.
mafaðaq mapa buna masa kawi.
S.TRANSL: I know how to carry sweet potatoes and firewood on my back.

S.FORM: ma-faðaq pa-tun-ruða masa pitʔia.
mafaðaq patunruða masa pitʔia.
S.TRANSL: I know how to steer a boat, and to cook.

S.FORM: ma-faðaq ma-didir paðay masa q<m>aʃiʃi ðaʃuq.
mafaðaq madidir paðay masa qmaʃiʃi ðaʃuq.
S.TRANSL: I know how to husk rice and sift rice.

S.FORM: uka-yða sa ina ama, numa ma-kasim a t<un>maða.
ukayða sa ina ama, numa makasim a tunmaða.
S.TRANSL: Having no mother or father, then (one is) sad listening (to the songs).

S.FORM: numa maniun ya miku-ki-náy, u-tusi-wan maniun mita a taun, m-ara sa fa-finʃiq a paðay, buna, ɬari, suksuk, makamun pu-náy maɬuyða.
numa maniun ya mikukináy, utusiwan maniun mita a taun, mara sa fafinʃiq a paðay, buna, ɬari, suksuk, makamun punáy maɬuyða.
S.TRANSL: If you (pl) like to live here, go to our houses to bring the seeds of rice, sweet potatoes, taros, ginger (and) pepper to plant here.

S.FORM: paʃtay mu-náy sa ayuði numa aðaðak a-tiʃ-an maqa a-ma-kaliŋkin sa but.
paʃtay munáy sa ayuði numa aðaðak atiʃan maqa amakaliŋkin sa but.
S.TRANSL: All men and boys must come to have (their sleeves) rubbed to stay healthy.

S.FORM: numa i-náy-ða yaku tu min-faðaq maʃ-babiar numa min-paraw numa ma-qa-quyaʃ.
numa ináyða yaku tu minfaðaq maʃbabiar numa minparaw numa maqaquyaʃ.
S.TRANSL: And here I learned how to strike (the ground) with a pestle, dance and sing.

S.FORM: numa sa ma-puði-puði a qnuan mu-saðum, ma-kuna maŋ-kaθi, numa uka-yða ʃaktu-n.
numa sa mapuðipuði a qnuan musaðum, makuna maŋkaθi, numa ukayða ʃaktun.
S.TRANSL: Then the white deer went into the water, going over to the other side, and then disappeared.

S.FORM: yutu s suma wa θaw, numa suma wa θaw ʃ<uŋ>kaʃ.
yutu s suma wa θaw, numa suma wa θaw ʃuŋkaʃ.
S.TRANSL: Some people stayed there, while the others were afraid.

S.FORM: sa suma ʃ<uŋ>kaʃ mapa-ʔuʃa, numa sa suma mapa-ʔu-ʃuqiʃ.
sa suma ʃuŋkaʃ mapaʔuʃa, numa sa suma mapaʔuʃuqiʃ.
S.TRANSL: Some were frightened and ran away, while the others returned.

S.FORM: m<in>aɬi-ʔaðaðak-iða makθin a qali, m-uʃa-yða mu-buhat.
minaɬiʔaðaðakiða makθin a qali, muʃayða mubuhat.
S.TRANSL: Ten days after having a baby, (the mother) goes to work.

S.FORM: numawan antu ma-kaliŋkin sa but.
numawan antu makaliŋkin sa but.
S.TRANSL: (She is), therefore, not healthy.

S.FORM: numa puʃa-n yamin, numawan manʃa sa funfun ɬay itan.
numa puʃan yamin, numawan manʃa sa funfun ɬay itan.
S.TRANSL: Then we released him, so they brought seeds as gifts to us.

S.FORM: ya ma-ʔania, numawan ðay-n sa θaw, a-malan-ta-tnur.
ya maʔania, numawan ðayn sa θaw, amalantatnur.
S.TRANSL: If capable (of shooting, they) were then asked to compete by the people.

S.FORM: maqa ya s<m>apuk sa ɬkaribuʃ, ma-θuaw undu-an.
maqa ya smapuk sa ɬkaribuʃ, maθuaw unduan.
S.TRANSL: Because (he) was very capable when (he) was catching wild animals.

S.FORM: maqa a-saran-an ya mu-ʃuqiʃ, pa-tqa-tqal-an.
maqa asaranan ya muʃuqiʃ, patqatqalan.
S.TRANSL: (They) kept making marks so that (they) could find their way back.

S.FORM: numa iðáy ɬa-ɬawʃin a fafaw quθquθ-an minabút, maqa antu a-m-utun, maqa a-ma-daqri ya iðáy a fa ɬawʃin-an.
numa iðáy ɬaɬawʃin a fafaw quθquθan minabút, maqa antu amutun, maqa amadaqri ya iðáy a fa ɬawʃinan.
S.TRANSL: Then the top of this swing is tied with rice straw, so that (it) won't break, so that this creeper swing will be smooth when swung.

S.FORM: maqa ma-tiŋ-qaran mun-ɬawʃin, maqa antu ma-qirið ya mu-buhat.
maqa matiŋqaran munɬawʃin, maqa antu maqirið ya mubuhat.
S.TRANSL: To go swinging so that one is happy, so that one does not get tired if/when working in the field.

S.FORM: numa ya m<in>u-lalu-yða, k<m>an afu.
numa ya minulaluyða, kman afu.
S.TRANSL: If/When the ceremony is over, (we) eat cooked rice.

S.FORM: m-ayaw sa θaw ya antu mu-tantu.
mayaw sa θaw ya antu mutantu.
S.TRANSL: (I would have been) sorry to people if (I had) not gone there.

S.FORM: myaðáy a malan-ta-tnur t<m>aðam ya tima sa ma-ʔania panaq sa iðáy ɬpaðiSan.
myaðáy a malantatnur tmaðam ya tima sa maʔania panaq sa iðáy ɬpaðiSan.
S.TRANSL: For such a practice, it was to test to see who was capable of shooting with an arrow.

S.FORM: maqa tu kahiwan ma-θuaw antu pidara ya s<m>iwsiw, antu ma-rarabaða.
maqa tu kahiwan maθuaw antu pidara ya smiwsiw, antu mararabaða.
S.TRANSL: People in the past took a magic (a ritual ceremony) very seriously; they did not allow it to be slighted.

S.FORM: iðáy binanawʔað, ya itiða sa rarifið, ʃi-na-haðiʃ-uan, kanun-iða suma wa binanawʔað ya ɬquðan.
iðáy binanawʔað, ya itiða sa rarifið, ʃinahaðiʃuan, kanuniða suma wa binanawʔað ya ɬquðan.
S.TRANSL: When the wooden plate of ancestors arrives, women should stay away, in case someone should be pregnant.

S.FORM: numa mataŋ-kaktun-iða, parʃian ya ma-qa-quyaʃ ʃa-ʃayla wa quyaʃ.
numa mataŋkaktuniða, parʃian ya maqaquyaʃ ʃaʃayla wa quyaʃ.
S.TRANSL: When all is over, to keep singing and dancing for the ritual ceremony is forbidden.

S.source: PDF p. 399; printed p. 406; footnote 7 example (1)
S.FORM: a muʃa iDa yaku ya saqaDi.
a muʃa iDa yaku ya saqaDi.
S.TRANSL: I'll leave this noon.

S.source: PDF p. 399; printed p. 406; footnote 7 example (2)
S.FORM: ya ʃaʃanu maθuaw waDaqan maharbuk.
ya ʃaʃanu maθuaw waDaqan maharbuk.
S.TRANSL: In the morning the lake is very foggy.

S.source: PDF p. 399; printed p. 406; footnote 7 example (3)
S.FORM: hadana ita iDa ya aDaDak.
hadana ita iDa ya aDaDak.
S.TRANSL: Let's adopt a child.
